definition: In this source, dependent groups are participant groups made up of people who are dependent on a substance, specifically codeine-containing cough syrup, and are compared with nondependent control participants. The term identifies a research group by dependence status rather than describing a general type of group.

reasons: The definition gives the wrong sense of the term: the packet uses “dependent groups” in a statistical/comparative sense (“controls and CCS-dependent groups”), not as a label for people dependent on a substance.
The substance-specific explanation and the claim that the term identifies a research group by dependence status rather than a general type of group are not supported by the packet.
The definition adds an unsupported example (“codeine-containing cough syrup”) as if it were the meaning of the term rather than a study-specific participant description.

The definition’s final claim (“The term identifies a research group by dependence status rather than describing a general type of group.”) is an interpretive/generalization that is not explicitly supported by the provided packet text.
